{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Patch testing requires 3 additional visits not shown in SoA",
      "quote": "Patients will be called to the site for 3 visits for the patch testing",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The SoA only shows a single 'Patch testing' at V1a, but the text requires 3 separate visits for application and two readings. This is a significant patient burden and scheduling complexity not reflected in the schedule.",
      "fix": "Add the 3 patch test visits to the SoA or clarify that V1a encompasses multiple visits."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing washout for topical JAK inhibitors may be too short",
      "quote": "1 week for TCS/TCI /topical JAK inhibitor/crisaborole application",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Topical JAK inhibitors have a longer half-life and may require longer washout to avoid false negatives; 1 week may be insufficient, risking protocol amendment or invalid results.",
      "fix": "Consider extending washout for topical JAK inhibitors to 2-4 weeks based on pharmacology."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing reading window is tight and may be hard to meet",
      "quote": "Appointment 2 (reading of results at day 2): the patches will be removed, and reading will be taken 20 to 30 minutes after removal of the patches.",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The 20-30 minute window after removal is very tight and may be difficult for sites to schedule precisely, especially with multiple patients.",
      "fix": "Allow a broader window (e.g., 20-60 minutes) for reading after removal."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing may require reading after day 7, adding unscheduled visits",
      "quote": "In some patients a reading after day 7 may be taken when the clinical history strongly supports sensitization.",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "This additional reading is not captured in the SoA and may require extra site visits, increasing patient burden and site workload.",
      "fix": "Add a note in the SoA for possible additional patch test reading visits."
    },
    {
      "title": "Vital signs and labs at EOS may be unnecessary burden",
      "quote": "Vital signs | X |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  | X | X | X | X",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Vital signs and labs (hematology, chemistry, urinalysis) are performed at EOS (V11) which is 12 weeks after EOT; this may be unnecessary for safety follow-up and adds burden.",
      "fix": "Consider removing labs and vital signs at EOS unless required by protocol for long-term safety."
    },
    {
      "title": "Injection training/observation at V3 and V4 may be redundant",
      "quote": "Injection training/ observation |  |  | X | X | X |  | X |  | X |  |  |  |  |",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Training/observation is done at every dosing visit (V2, V3, V4, V6, V8). After initial training, observation may not be needed at every visit, adding site time.",
      "fix": "Limit observation to first few doses and then only as needed."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patient diary training at V1 and V2 may be duplicative",
      "quote": "Patient diary training | X |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Training is done at screening and again at baseline; this may be redundant and could be consolidated to reduce patient burden.",
      "fix": "Consider training only at screening or baseline, not both."
    },
    {
      "title": "Photographs at EOS may be unnecessary",
      "quote": "Photograph areas of atopic hand or foot dermatitis (select sites) |  |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X | X |  | X",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Photographs are taken at baseline, EOT, and EOS. EOS is 12 weeks after EOT; capturing photos at EOS may not add value and adds burden.",
      "fix": "Consider removing photographs at EOS unless needed for long-term assessment."
    }
  ]
}
